blocks.content: 9.1 Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 establishes the statutory powers of SEBI to regulate Indian securities markets.
The SEBI Takeover Code (SAST Regulations, 2011) outlines rules regarding substantial acquisition of shares, voting rights, and open offer triggers.
The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 restrict connected persons from trading based on Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI).

cells: SEBI established as statutory body on 30 January 1992 (statutory powers); originally created 12 April 1988 (non-statutory)
Protect interests of investors in securities; promote and regulate securities market
Registration of market intermediaries; prohibition of insider trading and fraudulent practices; inspection; adjudication; civil monetary penalties
No person with Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) can trade or communicate UPSI; trading window; pre-clearance
Market manipulation; price rigging; mis-selling; creating artificial volumes; churning
Appeals against SEBI orders; SAT Presiding Officer = retired High Court Judge; further appeal to Supreme Court
SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations; listed company disclosure norms; corporate governance

rows: Statutory powers, market regulation, and investor protection
Substantial acquisition of shares, voting rights, and takeovers
Prevention of insider trading and safeguarding UPSI

cells: Acquisition of 25% or more voting rights in target company; or change of control
Minimum 26% of total shares from public shareholders
Existing shareholder with 25–75% can acquire additional 5% per year without making open offer
Voluntarily offer to acquire additional 10%+ of shares with intent to consolidate
Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers; ensures fair treatment of minority shareholders
Competition Commission of India approval required if thresholds met (combinatiom control thresholds)

items: Pay attention to the exact year of enactment for the SEBI Act (1992) and subsequent regulatory updates.
Questions frequently test open offer threshold limits under the SAST Regulations, 2011.
Understand the key definitions of UPSI and 'Connected Persons' under the PIT Regulations, 2015.

cells: Information relating to company not generally available which materially affects price: financial results, dividends, M&A, changes in key management, major contracts
Connected person who is in possession of UPSI; includes directors, KMPs, employees, and persons deemed connected
Period during which insiders are prohibited from trading; closed around scheduled disclosure events; compliance officer manages
Insiders must obtain pre-clearance before trading above threshold value even during open trading window
Companies must maintain digital database of persons sharing UPSI; cannot be tampered
Section 15G SEBI Act: Rs.25 crore or 3x profits from trade, whichever is higher; criminal prosecution possible under Section 24
